h1: The 7 Best Printers for Occasional Use, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers for Occasional Use: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 printers for people who print a few pages a month, compared on upfront cost, ink drying, scanning and photo output.
summary: The HP DeskJet 4355 is the best printer for occasional use because it is cheap, wireless and does print, copy and scan. Canon's PIXMA TS6520 is the one to buy if you want an on-unit status display, the TR4720 suits people who scan paperwork, and the MT610Pro is the only inkless option.
intro: The expensive part of owning a printer you rarely use is not the printer. It is the ink that dries, the cleaning cycles that burn through cartridges, and the replacement unit you buy after a year in a drawer. Buy for the drawer months, not the print month: a cheap printer that clogs after eight weeks ends up costing more than a dearer one that wakes cleanly.

So we ranked seven models for low upfront cost, idle-time behavior and ease of use, not for pages per minute. Every unit here sits under about $200, and one skips ink entirely. Listing data is thin on speed and yield, so we stick to what is documented. That is the logic behind every placement here.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One
products.verdict: The low-cost wireless all-in-one that suits a few prints a month.
products.description:
HP's DeskJet 4355 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one in the $50 to $100 range, with a compact body and a 3-month Instant Ink trial in the box. It handles print, copy and scan, which covers the occasional chores of forms, shipping labels and school sheets.

Our top spot comes down to economics. A printer used a handful of times a month should cost little to buy and little to leave idle, and the DeskJet is the lowest-priced of the full-featured models here. Canon's TS6520 adds a display, but you pay for hardware you rarely touch.

Buy it for a household that prints in bursts. Be careful with the Instant Ink trial: it is a subscription that bills after the trial unless you cancel, and a rarely used printer is usually better off with ordinary cartridges.
products.idealFor: Households printing a handful of pages a month.
products.skipIf: You want a screen showing ink and status.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Inkjet
products.verdict: A 1.42-inch OLED display makes ink and error checks painless between long gaps.
products.description:
The PIXMA TS6520 is a wireless color inkjet with a built-in copier and scanner, an intuitive control panel and a 1.42-inch OLED display. It is the only model here with a screen on the unit.

The display is why it ranks second. When a printer sits idle for weeks, the first job on return is working out whether it is ready, low on ink or showing a fault, and an OLED beats a blinking light. Against the HP DeskJet it costs the same range but adds this feedback.

Buy it if you hate cryptic errors. The compromise is that a 1.42 inch display is small, and you will still run a cleaning cycle after a long gap since it is a standard inkjet.
products.idealFor: Occasional users who want to see printer status at a glance.
products.skipIf: You never look at the printer between jobs.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One
products.verdict: Phone-friendly printing plus a scanner for the odd small stack of documents.
products.description:
Canon's TR4720 is a compact wireless all-in-one with mobile printing support and a built-in fax, which is a legacy feature most people will skip. It is in the $50 to $100 bracket and ships in white.

It ranks third because document handling is the use case: forms, receipts and the odd contract that needs scanning. It sits under the TS6520 only because it lacks a display, and above the TS6420 because it costs less.

Buy it for a home office that scans more than it prints. The fax is a throwback you will almost certainly never use, and there is no automatic document feeder listed, so every page goes on the glass by hand.
products.idealFor: Occasional users who scan a few documents now and then.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6420 All-in-One Wireless
products.verdict: A step up in photo output for the person who prints a handful of pictures.
products.description:
The Canon TS6420 is a wireless all-in-one with photo-capable output and a cartridge-based ink system, in a compact design in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks fourth for photo quality on infrequent prints, where an occasional family photo or school project matters more than document speed. The extra spend over the TR4720 buys that photo ability, not scanning convenience.

It suits someone who prints photos a few times a year. Keep in mind that cartridge-based inkjets can dry out if left idle, so run a short print monthly, and expect to buy replacement cartridges at ordinary retail cost instead of a bulk-ink design.

products.name: MT610Pro Inkless Portable Thermal Printer
products.verdict: No ink or toner at all, which removes the dried-nozzle problem entirely.
products.description:
The MT610Pro is an inkless thermal printer that prints 8.5 x 11 inch US Letter or A4 pages at 300 DPI over Bluetooth, working with iOS, Android and laptops. It is portable and lists in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It lands fifth because it fixes the main complaint of occasional printing, which is ink that dries out between uses, by having none. The price is capability: thermal paper is monochrome, fades with heat and light, and does not feel like plain office paper.

Choose it for travel and for the person who prints something twice a year. Skip it for anything you need to keep for years or hand over as a formal document.
products.idealFor: Very infrequent printers who hate ink maintenance.
products.skipIf: You need color or archival prints.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Inkjet
products.verdict: A 1-year warranty and easy setup at the lowest price tier.
products.description:
The PIXMA TS4320 is a compact wireless color inkjet with a built-in copier and scanner, easy setup and a 1 year limited warranty, all in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It ranks sixth because it is the stripped model: no display, no photo-focused output. The 1-year warranty is the useful differentiator, since an inexpensive inkjet that sits idle can fail early and you get a window to claim.

Pick it for dorms or a spare room where price matters most. A basic printer like this has the same idle-time cleaning needs as the rest, so print a test page at least once a month.
products.idealFor: Dorms and spare rooms where price matters most.
products.skipIf: You want a display or photo features.

products.name: Canon PIXMA MG3620 Wireless All-in-One
products.verdict: Built around printing from a phone or tablet, but with no document feeder.
products.description:
The MG3620 is a wireless color all-in-one with an emphasis on mobile and tablet printing and a cartridge-based ink system. It has no automatic document feeder and sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It finishes last because it costs more than the DeskJet and TR4720 without a standout feature to justify it. Phone printing is now common across the whole group. It trails the TR4720 because its mobile focus does not offset the missing feeder.

It is worth it only if you find it at a good price and print mostly from a phone. Everyone else should buy the HP or the TR4720 for less.
products.idealFor: People who print mostly from a phone or tablet.
products.skipIf: You want the best value in the group.

whatMatters.detail: Inkjet nozzles clog when a printer sits for weeks, forcing cleaning cycles that waste ink. Cartridge-based models like the Canon TS6420 are prone to it. The MT610Pro avoids it with thermal printing, so check the technology before you assume cost per page. Each wake-up cleaning pushes ink through the head, so a monthly one-page print is cheaper than letting it dry out.

Some HP printers include a trial of a monthly ink plan, as the DeskJet 4355 does for 3 months. These plans bill per page tier, and a low-volume user can end up paying for pages they do not print. Cancel before the trial ends unless you print often. Read the plan table before enabling it; a tier with more pages than you print is the usual trap.

A flatbed scanner handles one page at a time. An automatic document feeder handles stacks, but the Canon MG3620 explicitly lacks one. Check the listing for a feeder if you scan multi-page taxes or contracts. A single-page flatbed scan is fine for a form or ID, but multi-page tax packets quickly become a chore.

A small screen on the printer tells you what is wrong without hunting through an app. The Canon TS6520's 1.42-inch OLED is the only one listed here. It is a small feature, but it saves time after months of idle. It shows ink levels and paper jams on the machine, so you do not need the phone app after a long gap.

Thermal printers heat special paper to form an image, with no ink at all. They suit receipts, labels and quick pages, but output is single-color and can fade. Inkjets give color and standard paper at the price of maintenance. Thermal paper is a recurring cost too, and receipts fade in sunlight, so keep a color inkjet for anything you plan to file.

howToChoose.intro: Frequency decides whether ink or thermal makes sense.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Color, normal paper and cartridges that dry out if left idle. Picks: HP DeskJet 4355, Canon TS6520, TR4720, TS6420.

cards.label: Thermal
cards.text: No ink, monochrome output on special paper. Pick: MT610Pro.

howToChoose.note: Choose inkjet for color and normal paper, thermal if you print twice a year.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Low upfront cost, wireless printing from a phone and a warranty, in a compact body that fits a dorm.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: Canon TS4320 for the 1-year warranty, HP DeskJet 4355 for the lowest cost.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print photos or want clear status feedback. The Canon TS6420 or TS6520 earn the extra cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print forms and labels only. The HP DeskJet or Canon TS4320 is enough.

faq.q: Will these work with my phone?
faq.a: Yes, all are wireless, and the Canon TR4720 and MG3620 specifically list mobile printing support. The MT610Pro connects by Bluetooth to iOS, Android and laptops. The MT610Pro needs the app and paper installed, but no ink.

Leaving the HP DeskJet's Instant Ink trial running. It converts to a paid plan, and a low-volume printer rarely uses enough pages to benefit. Cancel the plan in your HP account before the trial ends if monthly volume is low.

faq.q: Is an inkless printer worth it over an inkjet?
faq.a: For a few pages a year, yes. The MT610Pro never clogs, but prints are monochrome on thermal paper, so keep an inkjet like the TS4320 for color work. A thermal print suits a label or a form, not a photo.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Plug it in, install the cartridges, then connect through the maker's app. The Canon TS4320 lists easy setup, and the TS6520's display guides you through it. Run the first alignment page after installing cartridges.

faq.q: How do I keep it from drying out?
faq.a: Print one color page a month and keep the printer powered down normally. Idle clogging mainly hits cartridge models like the Canon TS6420, MG3620 and TS4320. A monthly page keeps the nozzles wet, and a long gap tends to produce streaks.

Almost certainly not. The Canon TR4720 includes legacy fax, but you can send documents by email or a phone scanning app, and there is no feeder on that model anyway. A phone scanning app covers most scan jobs a fax would handle.

finalTake: The HP DeskJet 4355 is the printer to buy for light household use. Spend a bit more on the Canon TS6520 if you want a status screen, pick the TR4720 for scanning, or choose the MT610Pro if you print so rarely that ink is a liability. Cancel any ink subscription trial, and print one page a month to keep nozzles clear.
